skills.name: Growth of firms: internal growth and measures

note.text: Internal or organic growth expands a firm’s own operations, for example by adding capacity, products or outlets. It can be financed through retained profit, new owners’ funds or borrowing; internal growth does not mean finance must come only from retained earnings. Firm size can be measured by output, employees, assets or sales, which may rank firms differently. Profit is not identical to size. Compare the same measure and period when calculating a growth rate.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish size measures, calculate growth and explain how internal expansion can be financed. Builds on: scale economies, diseconomies and financing. Leads to: external growth through mergers and acquisitions.

sections.heading: Understand the economics
sections.text: Internal or organic growth expands a firm’s own operations, for example by adding capacity, products or outlets. It can be financed through retained profit, new owners’ funds or borrowing; internal growth does not mean finance must come only from retained earnings. Firm size can be measured by output, employees, assets or sales, which may rank firms differently. Profit is not identical to size. Compare the same measure and period when calculating a growth rate.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: A fictional Bamenda bakery adds its own oven and expands production without buying another enterprise. It may employ more workers and produce more units, but the larger output does not guarantee a higher profit if costs also rise. A rise in sales value can reflect price changes rather than an equal rise in physical output.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Name the measure, find the absolute change and divide by the original value for a percentage. State whether a change is organic or comes from combining firms. Assess demand, funds and management capacity before treating an expansion target as feasible.

cards.idea: Distinguish these features before judging a business.
example: internal growth: expansion through the firm’s own operations rather than combining with another business.
retained earnings: profits kept in the business rather than distributed.
size measure: a specified indicator such as output, employment or assets.
growth rate: the change relative to the original value, expressed as a percentage.

cards.idea: Use the stated case evidence to identify the economic feature.

cards.idea: Explain a consequence instead of assuming every option has the same effect.

retained earnings: Only profit retained after relevant costs is retained earnings.
size measure: Prices as well as quantity can change sales value.
growth rate: The original value is the base for the standard percentage increase.
